title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Media and Public Statements
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal is handling a highly publicized dog-bite case in Small Claims Court. A reporter asks the paralegal for comment. What is the ethical boundary for the paralegal's statement to the media?
options: The paralegal may say anything they wish, as freedom of expression supersedes the Rules of Conduct.
The paralegal must not comment at all while the matter is before the courts.
The paralegal may comment, but must not make public statements that infringe on the client's interests, confidentiality, or prejudice the administration of justice.
The paralegal can express personal opinions on the merits of the case but cannot mention the opposing party's name.
questions.explain: Rule 8.04 states that paralegals may communicate with the media, provided they do not infringe upon the practitioner's obligations to the client (confidentiality, best interests), the profession, or the courts, and they must avoid prejudicing the fair trial of a matter.
